adaptive_step_adaptive_phase_correlation.statement: same scenario, same noisy data, with adaptive_step=True (zuo2016's Eq. 16 rule) instead of the fixed ramp -- a real, reproducible improvement at this noise level, validated across 8 random seeds (8/8 favored adaptive_step, not itself in this registry since a multi-seed statistic isn't a single deterministic number)

adaptive_step_fixed_ramp_phase_correlati.statement: phase_correlation with the default fixed exponential-ramp step schedule, at heavy Poisson noise (peak_photon_count=3) and 400 iterations -- enough noise/cycles for zuo2016's described failure mode to manifest (an earlier pass at lighter noise and fewer iterations found no clean difference)

chromatic_shift_no_injection_error_px.statement: same scenario, red-vs-green pair (NO shift injected) -- sanity/negative-control number confirming the diagnostic doesn't report a spurious shift when there isn't one

chromatic_shift_recovery_error_px.statement: euclidean pixel error between chromatic_diagnostics.measure_lateral_shift_px's measured blue-vs-green shift and a known 2.0/-1.5px lateral shift injected into blue's true object before reconstruction -- validated synthetically since no real lab data exists in this Codespace yet

epry_corrected_phase_correlation.statement: same scenario, reconstructed with EPRY pupil recovery (recover_pupil=True) instead of assuming the ideal pupil -- a real but modest improvement, not a full fix

epry_paper_scale_baseline_phase_correlat.statement: same no-aberration scenario as epry_small_scale_*, but at a scale close to ou2014's own real demonstration (225 LEDs, 64x64px instead of 12x12, object spatial frequency kept physically comparable)

epry_paper_scale_corrected_phase_correla.statement: same paper-scale scenario, with recover_pupil=True -- the small-scale regression does NOT reproduce here, confirming it is a small-testbed/low-data-redundancy artifact, not a general EPRY failure or an implementation bug

epry_recovered_pupil_phase_correlation.statement: correlation between the EPRY-recovered pupil's phase and the true injected aberration's phase -- confirms EPRY identifies the actual aberration, not just 'helps the object by coincidence'

epry_small_scale_baseline_phase_correlat.statement: phase_correlation for the blue (470nm) channel on this project's small 9x9-LED/12x12px synthetic testbed, NO aberration present (ideal pupil) -- already reconstructs well without any pupil correction

epry_small_scale_corrected_phase_correla.statement: same scenario, with recover_pupil=True -- EPRY REGRESSES this already-healthy channel at this small testbed scale, even with no real aberration to correct

epry_uncorrected_phase_correlation.statement: phase_correlation assuming the ideal (unaberrated) pupil, when a real defocus aberration (Zernike mode 4, ou2014's own dominant real-microscope aberration) is actually present in the optics

exact_k_gradient_descent_phase_correlati.statement: same exact-k data, gradient descent with the matched continuous-k model (amplitude loss, 100 iterations, reconstruct_gradient_descent). Conversely, giving it a bin-rounded LED grid on exact-k data drops it to ~0.09 (tests/test_gd_solver_pipelines.py docstring, not in this registry): real LED position accuracy is probably the dominant unknown for any solver

exact_k_wirtinger_phase_correlation.statement: phase_correlation of the Wirtinger flow (200 epochs, bin-rounded k model) on captures simulated with the EXACT unrounded LED k (jc.simulate_lr_stack_continuous), green, 16px crops, noiseless -- the inverse-crime caveat: older fake captures round k to a bin (the very model the Wirtinger flow inverts), which hides this failure on data like real hardware would produce

five_percent_contrast_object_phase_corre.statement: reconstruction phase_correlation for the SAME phase field with just 5% amplitude contrast added -- demonstrates how much a small amount of amplitude structure matters to this solver

gd_noise_green_peak20_gradient_descent_a.statement: same scenario, same noisy data, Adam gradient descent with loss="amplitude" (100 iterations). Across 8 seeds (scripts/sweep_gd_vs_wf_noise.py) the paired gain over the Wirtinger flow is +0.462 +/- 0.026 SE in green (8/8) and +0.472 +/- 0.013 in red (8/8); the intensity-L2 and Poisson-NLL losses do not hold up under noise, and blue fails for every solver at peak <= 20

gd_noise_green_peak20_wirtinger_phase_co.statement: phase_correlation of the Wirtinger flow (200 epochs), green channel, Poisson noise at peak photon count 20, seed 0, bin-aligned k, 16px crops -- the exact reproducible seed of an 8-seed sweep (not itself in this registry since a multi-seed statistic isn't a single deterministic number)

gd_noiseless_blue_gradient_descent_phase.statement: same scenario and data, Adam gradient descent on the intensity loss (100 iterations, joint_calibration.reconstruct_and_calibrate, calibrate_leds=False) -- converges where the Wirtinger flow does not. NOISELESS, one object, one geometry: NOT a general advantage (see the amplitude-loss noise entries)

gd_noiseless_blue_wirtinger_phase_correl.statement: phase_correlation of the Wirtinger flow (400 epochs) on the blue channel, noiseless, 16px crops, 9x9 LEDs, bin-aligned k so both solvers see identical information -- it never converges, even with 4x the iterations (tests/test_gradient_descent_vs_wirtinger.py)

led_calibration_scale_recovery_error.statement: absolute error between the LED spectral-correlation calibration's fitted scale factor and a known injected misalignment's true scale factor, given a good object spectrum estimate

lena_map_gd_phase_correlation_peak_100.statement: phase_correlation of amplitude-loss gradient descent (100 iterations) on the Lena(amplitude)+Map(phase) object (phase max 0.3*pi), green, 9x9 LEDs, 32px crops, bin-aligned k, Poisson noise at peak photon count 100, seed 0 -- the phase is NOT recovered at this photon budget. Needs the images in test_objects.DEFAULT_DATA_DIR (outside the repo)

lena_map_gd_phase_correlation_peak_1000.statement: same scenario at peak photon count 1000 -- the phase starts to become recoverable from ~1000 peak photons (scripts/sweep_lena_map_noise_and_redundancy.py part A; 4 seeds per peak, not in this registry). The redundancy-vs-LED-overlap effect at fixed canvas is not separated here

multispectral_thickness_correlation.detail: see tests/test_multispectral_end_to_end.py for the identical scenario as an assertion
multispectral_thickness_correlation.statement: correlation between the milestone-2 coupled pipeline's recovered sample-thickness field and the true field, on a synthetic 3-channel dispersion object reconstructed through the actual Wirtinger flow solver (not injected phase)

phase_only_object_phase_correlation.statement: reconstruction phase_correlation for a UNIFORM-amplitude (pure phase) object -- the baseline solver's known weak point, see docs/roadmap_agentic_multispectral_pipeline.md section 1 point 6

ransac_plain_fit_rotation_error_rad.statement: absolute rotation error (radians) of a plain least-squares similarity-transform fit with 10% of points corrupted to implausible positions

ransac_robust_fit_rotation_error_rad.statement: same scenario, same points, fit with fit_similarity_transform_ransac instead -- the outlier-rejection improvement added to LED calibration

resumen_R_Ainit.statement: Rojo 25/09 set 3, método A+init: error de predicción de LEDs no vistos, promedio de 5 folds (cv.A+init.mean; 1 = no mejor que una constante)

resumen_R_sinfpm.statement: El mismo error sin reconstruir, prediciendo desde la imagen inicial (nofpm.mean)

resumen_abbe_verde_um.reproduce: lambda/(2 NA) con lambda = 0.53 um y NA = 0.07
resumen_abbe_verde_um.statement: Límite de resolución (Abbe) del objetivo 2.5x NA 0.07 en luz verde, en µm

resumen_adjunto_error.statement: Error relativo del operador inverso original (common.py de ptyco-full-simulator) frente al adjunto exacto del operador directo (0 = correcto)

resumen_centro_col.statement: Captura 12/12/2025: columna del eje óptico ajustada con el brillo por LED (main_z76_poly4.col)

resumen_centro_fila.statement: Captura 12/12/2025: fila del eje óptico ajustada con el brillo por LED (main_z76_poly4.row; la columna es main_z76_poly4.col)

resumen_frc_real.statement: Rojo 25/09: coincidencia (FRC) entre las dos mitades de LEDs en la banda 0.222-0.45 1/µm, más allá del límite del objetivo (C2.frc_sel)

resumen_frc_sint.statement: La misma coincidencia entre mitades en la simulación de la captura (C2.frc_sel, método B)

resumen_frc_umbral.reproduce: clip(0.5 x FRC sintético, 0.143, 0.5), regla de results/captura_2026-09-25_red/criterios.md
resumen_frc_umbral.statement: Umbral de C2, fijado con la simulación antes de mirar los datos reales

resumen_leds_utiles_2409.statement: Captura 24/09, verde con enfoque verde, 100 ms: LEDs (de 169) con señal estructural/ruido > 3 (fórmula de results/captura_2026-09-24/stats_por_led/an.py)

resumen_leds_utiles_julio.statement: Captura 08/07/2026, verde, 1 ms: LEDs (de 182) con al menos 10 % del brillo del LED más brillante (channels.green.census.n_ge_10pct_peak)

resumen_paso_congelado_factor.statement: Cuántas veces más chico que el paso ePIE unitario era el paso de Wirtinger flow con recortes de 400 px (roadmap sección 6.9)

resumen_rgb_R_rojo.statement: RGB 28/09, rojo, A+init: error de predicción de LEDs no vistos (5 folds, C1_rojo)

resumen_rgb_banda_max.statement: RGB 28/09: correlación del brillo reconstruido entre colores dentro de la banda del objetivo (máximo de los tres pares; el mínimo es 0.18)

resumen_rgb_crudas_min.statement: RGB 28/09: correlación entre colores de la foto cruda (18,15), registrada (mínimo de rojo-verde y azul-verde)

resumen_rgb_frc_verde.statement: RGB 28/09, verde: coincidencia entre mitades de LEDs en la banda [2NA/lambda, 0.45] 1/µm (el rojo da 0.014 y el azul 0.009, mismo archivo)

resumen_rgb_sinfpm_rojo.statement: RGB 28/09, rojo: el mismo error sin reconstruir

resumen_rgb_todo_max.statement: RGB 28/09: la misma correlación con todo el espectro reconstruido (máximo de los tres pares)

resumen_set1_R.statement: Rojo 25/09 set 1 (otra zona), A+init: error de predicción de LEDs no vistos (C1.sel_mean)

resumen_set1_sinfpm.statement: Set 1: el mismo error sin reconstruir (C1.nofpm)

resumen_set1_sint_R.statement: Simulación con los niveles de señal y ruido del set 1 (muestra delgada): error de predicción de LEDs no vistos (sintetico.C1.sel_mean)

resumen_set1_sint_frc.statement: La misma simulación: coincidencia entre las dos mitades en la banda más allá del objetivo (sintetico.C2.frc_sel)

resumen_sint_amplitud.statement: Simulación sin ruido con la geometría real (2.5x, z = 75 mm, 100 iteraciones): correlación del brillo reconstruido con el de la muestra (runs[hoy_2.5x_z75, 100].amplitude_correlation)

resumen_sint_fase.statement: La misma simulación: correlación de la fase (runs[hoy_2.5x_z75, 100].phase_correlation)

resumen_sint_fase_z100.statement: La misma simulación con la matriz a 100 mm, es decir más solapamiento entre LEDs vecinos (runs[2.5x_z100, 100].phase_correlation)

resumen_solapamiento_pct.statement: Solapamiento entre las pupilas de dos LEDs vecinos en el espectro, z = 74 mm, en % del área

resumen_z115_R.statement: Rojo 25/09, método B con z = 115 mm: error de predicción de LEDs no vistos (results/captura_2026-09-25_red/out/tasks/real_B_z115.0_f*.json)

resumen_zeiss_um_px.statement: Tamaño de píxel en la muestra de la imagen de referencia Zeiss, en µm

suite_coverage.statement: checks.py pass/fail coverage for this project's correctness suite

tie_informed_init_baseline_phase_correla.statement: phase_correlation for a mixed-low/high-spatial-frequency phase object with the default zero-phase solver initialization

tie_informed_init_phase_correlation.statement: phase_correlation for the SAME object, initializing the solver with a Transport of Intensity Equation phase estimate instead of zero -- fixes the degenerate saddle point found in docs/roadmap_agentic_multispectral_pipeline.md section 1 point 6

unwrapping_error_reduction_factor.statement: how many times smaller the coupled (unwrap + dispersion-fit) pipeline's thickness RMSE is than a naive baseline that treats each channel's raw wrapped phase as already-unwrapped OPL, on a synthetic dispersion signal large enough to require real unwrapping
